headline_marked: OpenAI to release [[ChatGPT 5.6 to gov't-approved customers]] first
headline: OpenAI to release ChatGPT 5.6 to gov't-approved customers first
summary: OpenAI will initially only release ChatGPT 5.6 to government-approved customers. The new AI model will be rolled out in a staggered manner.
details: OpenAI plans to stagger the release of its new AI model, ChatGPT 5.6, with initial access limited to parties approved by the federal government. According to a report in The Information, federal leaders will be 'approving access customer by customer during this preview period,' followed by a more general release a 'couple of weeks later'.

The decision comes as the US government is expected to create a framework to standardize how it assesses new AI models. President Donald Trump signed an executive order earlier this month asking AI companies to participate in a voluntary federal review of their more powerful models before they are publicly released.

Several agencies are involved in directing the change in course from OpenAI, including the Office of the National Cyber Director and the Office of Science and Technology Policy, as well as involvement from Department of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.
caption:
Will you be able to use ChatGPT 5.6? Probably not at first.

OpenAI plans to stagger the release of its new AI model, ChatGPT 5.6, with initial access limited to parties approved by the federal government. According to a report in The Information, federal leaders will be 'approving access customer by customer during this preview period,' followed by a more general release a 'couple of weeks later'.

The decision comes as the US government is expected to create a framework to standardize how it assesses new AI models. President Donald Trump signed an executive order earlier this month asking AI companies to participate in a voluntary federal review of their more powerful models before they are publicly released.

Several agencies are involved in directing the change in course from OpenAI, including the Office of the National Cyber Director and the Office of Science and Technology Policy, as well as involvement from Department of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

headline_marked: Russia questions [[Apple's removal of Russian apps]] from US App Store
headline: Russia questions Apple's removal of Russian apps from US App Store
summary: Russia seeks explanation for app removals. Apple faces scrutiny.
details: Russia is seeking an explanation from Apple for the removal of Russian apps from the US App Store. The move has sparked scrutiny and concern.
The Russian government has taken notice of the app removals and is now seeking clarity on the matter. Apple has not publicly commented on the reason behind the removals.
This incident highlights the ongoing tensions between Russia and tech companies. Russia has previously clashed with companies over content and data storage.
caption:
What's behind Apple's removal of Russian apps?

Russia is seeking an explanation from Apple for the removal of Russian apps from the US App Store. The move has sparked scrutiny and concern.

The Russian government has taken notice of the app removals and is now seeking clarity on the matter. Apple has not publicly commented on the reason behind the removals.

This incident highlights the ongoing tensions between Russia and tech companies. Russia has previously clashed with companies over content and data storage.
